purpose: Primary-source and pinned local evidence for LIBS physical triage priors

facts_used: Observed relative intensities depend on source conditions and are generally not sensitivity corrected.
Transition probabilities carry accuracy grades and may be flagged as doubtful or intensity derived.
Optically thin emitted line power is proportional to upper-level population times A times photon energy.
Lines sharing an upper level therefore have a branching relation after wavelength and response correction.
Persistent neutral-argon anchors occur throughout the red and near infrared, including the detector groups near 696.54, 706.72, 763.51, 811.53, 826.45, and 842.46 nm.
The O I 777 nm components form one multiplet-scale observable, while the 844.6 nm group supplies an independent neutral-oxygen feature.
The McWhirter density criterion is necessary but insufficient for LTE in LIBS plasma.
Spatial and temporal gradients limit hard Saha-Boltzmann rejection rules.
Branching-ratio measurements require control of self-absorption, blends, and spectral response.
Resonance and low-lying LIBS lines can be strongly self-absorbed, invalidating naive intensity ratios.
LIBS curve-of-growth behavior links optical depth to saturation and self-absorption diagnostics.
Automated LIBS line selection should account for interference and line quality rather than raw database intensity alone.
Chance wavelength coincidences rise with line and feature density, motivating a local coincidence penalty.
928 rows have positive integrated areas and SNR at least 5 for both K resonance features.
Area-ratio 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles are 1.351270, 1.440607, and 1.527383; 926 of 928 fall outside plus or minus 20 percent of 2.006045.
This reused corpus has no independent certified composition and does not uniquely prove self-absorption.
The Fe session is useful for native-grid and nuisance checks but is not an independently certified Ar/O gas validation set.
